page: Amazon Web Services m8i.large is a general-purpose server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor featuring 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, which translates to 4.0 GB of memory per core. It features no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on external storage solutions, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks highlight a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The m8i.large demonstrates strong single-core performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2169.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. Conversely, multi-core metrics are weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2735.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core CPU performance rating of 2158.78. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, showing a poor read-only large block bandwidth of 22.61 GB/sec and a weak write large block bandwidth of 17.99 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-threaded execution, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that do not require high parallel processing or massive memory throughput. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving.
